Chapter 4: System Planning

4.1 Requirement Analysis & Data Gathering

Requirement engineering in this enterprise software internship followed a structured multi-source elicitation methodology. Elicitation combined semi-structured interviews with the industry mentor, structured consultations with the internal academic guide, observational studies of operational bottlenecks in manual spreadsheet logs, and comparative evaluation of ITIL v4 asset management paradigms. Requirements gathered were cataloged into an elicitation log and subsequently consolidated into functional specifications prioritized under the MoSCoW framework.

M1: Auth & Users JWT-based authentication, salted password hashing, 3-tier RBAC (Admin, IT Support, Employee), user lifecycle management. FR-01, FR-02, FR-03, FR-04 Must Have
M2: Assets Hardware asset inventory tracking, automatic tag generation (AST-YYYY-XXXX), atomic user allocation, lifecycle states. FR-05, FR-06, FR-07, FR-08, FR-09 Must Have
M3: Licenses Software seat tracking, seat allocation/release, 30-day expiry threshold computation, sensitive license key masking. FR-10, FR-11, FR-12, FR-20 Must Have
M4: Tickets Self-service ticket creation, 4-tier SLA urgency calculation, staff assignment, threaded comments, status workflow, resolution note. FR-13, FR-14, FR-15, FR-16 Must Have
M5: Analytics Role-customized KPI dashboards, real-time status distributions, append-only immutable audit trail, RFC 4180 CSV export. FR-17, FR-18, FR-19 Should Have

4.2 Time-line Chart & SOP Milestones

The 15-week internship curriculum was scheduled in strict compliance with VICAIT SOP Section 2.4 guidelines. Project execution was divided into four foundational phases punctuated by four formal institutional progress report evaluations. Figure 4.1 visualizes the schedule, while Table 4.3 outlines the week-by-week deliverable roadmap.

Table 4.3: 15-Week Project Plan as per VICAIT SOP Section 2.4
Week Project Phase Activity Description Formal Deliverable Actual Dates
W1–W2 Inception & Approval Internship registration, industry host onboarding, topic finalization, and initial project scope proposal approval. Approved Project Proposal (SOP 4.1)  
W3 Planning & Elicitation Interviews with mentor and IT staff, manual workflow observation, feasibility assessment, initial backlog synthesis. Requirement Log & Feasibility Matrix  
W4–W5 Analysis & Modeling Authoring IEEE-830 SRS, defining FR-01..FR-20, drafting DFD Level 0/1/2 and functional decomposition hierarchies. Progress Report I & SRS Document  
W6–W7 Architectural Design 3-tier architecture definition, MongoDB schema design, ER diagramming, class/sequence diagrams, UI wireframing. Database Schema & UI Design Blueprints  
W8 Mid-Term Review Backend API scaffolding, authentication engine completion, mid-term progress demo to institutional guide. Progress Report II & Milestone Demo  
W9–W10 Core Implementation Full implementation of M1–M5 (hardware tracking, software seats, ticket triage, audit logging, CSV reports). Progress Report III & Working Software  
W11–W12 Quality Assurance Automated test execution: 57 unit tests, 199 integration tests, 16 Playwright E2E journeys, latency benchmark runs. Test Suite (272 Tests, 87.16% Coverage)  
W13–W14 Documentation VICAIT SOP 50-page technical report drafting, user guide manual creation, logbook annexure consolidation. Progress Report IV & Draft Report  
W15 Evaluation & Defense Host organization sign-off, hard-binding, presentation preparation, comprehensive academic viva voce examination. Final Bound Report & Project Defense
